questions.solution_html:

  • Systematic Record of Transactions
  • Ignores Qualitative Factors

questions.question: / Explain how the business can apply the concept of a cash book in recording these transactions. Discuss its features and advantages . A small business wants to maintain accurate records of all its financial
questions.solution_html:
• A business can maintain a cash book to record all cash receipts and payments on a daily
  • basis. Every time cash is received, it is entered on the debit side, and every time cash is paid, it
  • is entered on the credit side. The cash book acts as both a journal (for recording) and a ledger
  • (for posting) for all cash transactions.
  • Features of a Cash Book
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: / transactions. Explain how the business can apply the double entry system of accounting in recording these transactions. Also, discuss the advantages and limitations . Paid to Syama Prasad Rs. 1,80,000
questions.solution_html:
• Double Entry System – Explanation, Advantages, and Limitations
  • Application of Double Entry System:A small business can use the double entry system
  • to record all financial transactions by ensuring that every transaction affects at least two
  • accounts—one debit and one credit.
  • Example: If the business purchases goods for cash: Purchases A/c — Debit,Cash A/c — Credit
  • This ensures that the accounting equation Assets = Liabilities + Capital always remains
  • balanced.
  • Advantages of Double Entry System

questions.question: / the role of a petty cash book in handling such transactions. Discuss its advantages and importance.
questions.solution_html:
• Role of a Petty Cash Book
  • A Petty Cash Book is used by a business to record small, frequent cash payments such as
  • postage, stationery, refreshments, travel expenses, and minor repairs.
  • Instead of recording every small transaction in the main cash book, the business maintains a
  • separate petty cash system, usually under the imprest system, where a fixed amount is given to
  • the petty cashier for small expenses.The petty cashier records each expense under proper heads
  • (postage, traveling, telephone, etc.) which makes tracking and controlling petty expenses simple
  • and efficient
  • Advantages of a Petty Cash Book
questions.final_answer: Advantages of a Petty Cash Book

questions.solution_html:
• A business can maintain a cash book to record all cash receipts and payments on a daily
  • basis. Every time cash is received, it is entered on the debit side, and every time cash is paid, it
  • is entered on the credit side. The cash book acts as both a journal (for recording) and a ledger
  • (for posting) for all cash transactions.

questions.question: / transactions. Explain how the business can apply the double entry system of accounting in recording these transactions. Also, discuss the advantages and limitations . Paid to Syama Prasad Rs. 1,80,000
questions.solution_html:
• Double Entry System – Explanation, Advantages, and Limitations
  • Application of Double Entry System:A small business can use the double entry system
  • to record all financial transactions by ensuring that every transaction affects at least two
  • accounts—one debit and one credit.
  • Example: If the business purchases goods for cash: Purchases A/c — Debit,Cash A/c — Credit
  • This ensures that the accounting equation Assets = Liabilities + Capital always remains
  • balanced.
  • Advantages of Double Entry System

questions.question: / the role of a petty cash book in handling such transactions. Discuss its advantages and importance.
questions.solution_html:
• Role of a Petty Cash Book
  • A Petty Cash Book is used by a business to record small, frequent cash payments such as
  • postage, stationery, refreshments, travel expenses, and minor repairs.
  • Instead of recording every small transaction in the main cash book, the business maintains a
  • separate petty cash system, usually under the imprest system, where a fixed amount is given to
  • the petty cashier for small expenses.The petty cashier records each expense under proper heads
  • (postage, traveling, telephone, etc.) which makes tracking and controlling petty expenses simple
  • and efficient
  • Advantages of a Petty Cash Book
questions.final_answer: Advantages of a Petty Cash Book
